text: Indirect regulation is often the only feasible tool available, because in many jurisdictions regulators lack full direct regulatory authority over hedge funds and can act only through the regulated entities they do control.
citation: Kaal, Indirect Regulation of Hedge Funds (2019). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3405660
abstract: Indirect regulation if often the only feasible regulatory tool for regulators seeking to lower risks associated with the hedge fund industry and protect investors and markets. In many jurisdictions, regulators do not have (full) direct regulatory authority over hedge funds.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: jurisdictions where regulators lack full direct authority over hedge funds
regulators have authority over broker dealers, prime brokers and affiliates
